claims.statement: The `libs/code` focused test target runs pytest with xdist, coverage, benchmark suppression, and sockets disabled except Unix sockets; package guidance requires deterministic network-free tests under `tests/unit_tests/`, automatic asyncio mode, and warnings treated as errors.

`RemoteAgent.aget_model_catalog()` binds catalog discovery to a thread workspace, posts purpose, recommendations, and current spec to the thread models endpoint, validates the response as `ModelCatalog`, and applies a 60-second timeout.

The catalog endpoint rejects an invalid request shape before workspace/model work, discovers in the bound workspace's saved model environment on a worker thread, applies profile overrides only for the main purpose, and distinguishes workspace conflict (409), invalid configuration/input (422), and unavailable/unexpected discovery failure (503).

Host-side catalog loading assembles available models and provider readiness, retains allowed enabled recommended/current specs, reports enabled known providers even when they have no discovered rows, omits disabled/disallowed entries, and isolates individual provider failures.

The strict catalog boundary carries only presentation data: profiles are filtered to an allowlisted scalar set with override provenance, while providers expose readiness and display/setup metadata without credential values or arbitrary configuration.

A server-backed selector uses the supplied catalog rather than local provider/config data, including for highlighting, label-based search, and selection; configured custom providers with no discovered models still route a typed spec to installation or authentication setup.

The selector focuses its filter before asynchronous loading, reapplies text entered during loading, abandons late data after dismissal, searches the full unfiltered list for a nonempty query, and keeps recent/current choices in the recommended view.

For a typed custom model, a selector checks `models.allowed` before provider installation or authentication; in a catalog-backed selector, bare or ambiguous/unrecognized provider prefixes are deferred to inference-host resolution instead of using local provider inference.

Selection routes missing provider packages to an install confirmation, missing regular credentials to an API-key prompt, and missing Codex credentials through a confirmation-gated OAuth flow; cancelled setup keeps the selector open and refreshes it.

`Ctrl+S` uses an explicit default scope and runs default validation/persistence asynchronously; it prevents overlapping requests, stores a canonical resolved spec only after validation, permits clearing an already stored unavailable selection, and guards against stale results after dismissal.

Metadata endpoint tests require malformed requests to fail before model construction, failed switches to preserve existing active model state, a bare switch to adopt the server-returned provider, and auxiliary selections to resolve in server context without changing the main model.

When dcode has a remote agent, the app loads catalogs and resolves proposed choices through that host; otherwise it uses a threaded bootstrap loader and disconnected resolution only for local identity/policy checking.

`LocalShellBackend` uses platform-specific process readers, routes timeout or cancellation through shared termination and cleanup, kills the POSIX process group when possible, and always closes captured pipes; a timeout response records whether cleanup actually stopped the command.

The POSIX and Windows process readers preserve incomplete output across timed-out polling attempts and require both captured-pipe completion and direct-process exit; the Windows reader polls pipes to avoid reader threads that can wait indefinitely for inherited writers.

Talon loads hooks only from the assistant home with no-follow regular-file checks, turns configuration read/parse failures into diagnostic snapshots, and creates a per-turn runtime that explicitly marks workspace hooks untrusted and unloaded.

A Talon child hook session shares its parent's hook runtime snapshot but receives a distinct thread, prompt, agent identity, and transcript context; fulfillment rejects requests whose snapshot or invocation context does not belong to the current turn.

Fresh Talon subagents are compiled with only explicit tool attachments and a fresh task context, retain MCP/subagent-control and applicable approval middleware, and child hooks omit stop events; unknown precompiled tool graphs are refused when an approval policy must be enforced.

Extras-status tests require all requirements of an extra to be installed, omit flattened composite extras, and enforce that non-composite optional dependencies are classified exactly once across the provider, sandbox, and standalone taxonomy.

Release-note automation derives release targets and writable changelog paths from the release-please registry, accepts only an internal open main-targeted release PR whose branch component and title agree, and rejects unsafe component/path configuration.

Release-note draft and apply operations revalidate release identity and head state, reject model output containing trusted markers or version headings, require a valid bot-authored draft, and recheck snapshots immediately before moving the release branch ref to prevent stale publication.
